name: min, max and pow return unknown rather than guessing at a side they could not work out
why: `min` and `max` are how a row states a BOUND on one of its own figures — a usage charge capped at a plan's ceiling, a balance floored at zero. There is no conditional in this language and booleans do not coerce to numbers, so without them a cap simply cannot be written. That makes their null discipline load-bearing: returning the other side when one is unknown would silently un-cap a figure that was supposed to be capped, and the number would look reasonable.

cases.why: A charge capped at the plan ceiling.
A balance floored at zero. Nothing owed is nothing, not a negative.

BOTH sides blank is ZERO, not unknown. This is the case that separates the two kinds of missing: a blank field reads as zero, so both bounds are genuinely known to be zero and the lower of them is zero.

But a bound that could not be WORKED OUT takes the whole thing to unknown. Returning `usage` here would report an uncapped charge as though it had been capped, which is the failure this rule exists to stop.
Either side, not just the right one.
Same discipline for max, so a floor cannot be lost the way a cap cannot.
pow, for compound growth and annualised returns.
A power that overflows decimal is unknown, not an exception. An OverflowException from inside a total is a 500 on a page somebody was only reading.
A negative base under a fractional exponent is NaN in double, and NaN is not a number anybody should see. Unknown.
min and max stay in decimal and are exact, unlike pow which goes through double. A cap must not move by a rounding error.
